House Edge Explained: Which Casino Games Give the Best Odds

Published August 20, 2026 · 7 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Every casino game is built with a mathematical edge in the house's favor — that's how casinos stay in business. But that edge varies a lot from game to game, and knowing the numbers is the single best tool you have for deciding where your entertainment budget goes furthest.

What "house edge" actually means

House edge is the average percentage of every bet a casino expects to keep over the long run. A 2% house edge means that, on average and over a very large number of bets, the casino keeps $2 of every $100 wagered — the other $98 cycles back to players as winnings. It's a long-run average, not a per-spin outcome: any single session can go well above or below it in either direction.

House edge by game (typical ranges)

Best odds

Blackjack (basic strategy)

~0.5% house edge with correct basic strategy — one of the lowest of any casino game.

Good odds

Baccarat (banker bet)

~1.06% house edge — simple rules, no strategy decisions required.

Moderate

Craps (pass line)

~1.4% house edge on the basic pass line bet; other craps bets vary widely, some far worse.

Moderate

European Roulette

~2.7% house edge (single zero). American roulette's extra double-zero pocket roughly doubles it to ~5.26%.

Wide range

Video poker

Anywhere from under 1% to 5%+ depending entirely on the specific pay table — see our video poker guide once published.

Highest

Slots

Typically 4–12%+ depending on the specific game — the widest range of any casino game, and the hardest for a player to identify in advance.

Why the same game can have different edges

Rule variations change the math significantly. In blackjack, whether the dealer hits or stands on a soft 17, how many decks are used, and payout ratios for a natural blackjack (3:2 vs. the worse 6:5) can shift the house edge by a percentage point or more. In roulette, a single extra pocket (American double-zero vs. European single-zero) nearly doubles the edge. Always check a game's specific rules before assuming a "typical" number applies.

Volatility isn't the same as house edge

A low house edge doesn't necessarily mean a "smoother" experience. Volatility (or variance) describes how much results swing session to session — a game can have a modest house edge but high volatility (big rare wins, frequent small losses), or a similar edge with low volatility (frequent small wins). Slots tend to be higher-volatility; blackjack and baccarat tend to be lower-volatility. Think about which pattern fits how you want to spend your session, not just the long-run percentage.

Takeaway: Games with player decisions — blackjack, video poker with correct strategy — tend to offer the best mathematical odds because skill affects the outcome. Pure chance games with no decisions, like slots and roulette, generally carry a higher built-in edge.
House edge describes long-run averages across millions of bets — it does not predict or guarantee any individual session's outcome. Treat every session as entertainment spending, not an investment; see our responsible gambling resources.
